books.section: A. Soviet-American Relations from Détente to Confrontation

stem: Which of the following best explains how Reagan's confrontational approach in the passage related to the arms-control agreements of his second term?

options.text: The pressure of the buildup helped bring the Soviets to negotiate the INF Treaty
The speech ended all negotiations, and no arms treaty was signed in the 1980s
options.misconception: The INF Treaty was signed in 1987, so negotiations did not end.

options.text: The speech convinced Congress to abolish the Strategic Defense Initiative
options.misconception: Congress did not abolish SDI; research on missile defense continued.

options.text: The speech led the Soviet Union to invade Afghanistan
options.misconception: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan happened in 1979, four years before the speech.

rationales.A: Background: Princeton notes the escalated arms race helped bring both sides to the bargaining table, since neither could afford its cost. In 1987 Reagan and Gorbachev signed the INF Treaty, eliminating an entire class of missiles.
rationales.B: The INF Treaty proves negotiations continued. Background: Reagan and Gorbachev met repeatedly and signed the treaty in December 1987.
rationales.C: SDI was never abolished by Congress. Background: the program stayed alive as a research effort through Reagan's presidency.
rationales.D: The dates run the wrong way. Background: Soviet troops entered Afghanistan in December 1979, before Reagan took office.
rationales.general:
1. Do not read the speech as the whole story. Reagan confronted first, then negotiated.
2. Background: the buildup, including the Strategic Defense Initiative, raised the cost of competing for a Soviet economy already under strain.
3. Background: Princeton notes the arms race helped bring both sides to the bargaining table, since neither could afford its cost.
4. In 1987 Reagan and Gorbachev signed the INF Treaty, eliminating an entire class of missiles.
Remember: pressure and negotiation were two halves of the same policy, not opposites.

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of President Ronald Reagan's address, March 8, 1983. Post-1929 material is paraphrased, not quoted.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of President Ronald Reagan's address to the National Association of Evangelicals, March 8, 1983: Reagan described the Soviet Union as the center of evil in the modern world. He warned Americans against treating the United States and the Soviet Union as equally at fault in the arms race, and he urged them to stand firm against a system he called the enemy of freedom and human dignity.
